# V15 evidence and hygiene audit

A scan of the committed VNX-DNA tree for evidence and hygiene problems, produced
by `tools/v15-evidence-scan.py`.

* Tree scanned: the committed file list (`git ls-files`) at commit `5b9ad9c` on
  branch `work/v15-t18`, worktree `/root/vnx-dna-lab/v15-t18`, plus this report
  once it is tracked.
* Scope: the committed files under `src/`, `tests/`, `docs/` and `experiments/`,
  plus `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`.
* The scan **reports**; it does not gate. It exits 0 even when it finds hits, and
  a hit is not automatically a defect. Every hit below is a line for a human to
  judge. This document does not judge them for you; section 5 records what a
  first pass of inspection saw.

## 1. What the script checks

Five categories, one per item in the brief.

**Category 1 - attribution.** AI-tool, assistant and model names, attribution
trailer phrases, and the agent scratch path, in committed file content *and* in
the commit messages of the committed history. Matching is on word boundaries, so
a longer word that merely ends with a trailer phrase is not read as a trailer,
and a phrase about overwriting is not read as an attribution phrase either. The
commit-message half of this category scans the whole committed history, not just
the tip.

**Category 2 - claims.** The words that assert DNA was synthesised, stored or
sequenced, that promise a lifetime, or that assert a superlative:
`synthesised`, `synthesized`, `synthesized-into-DNA`, `sequenced`, `guaranteed`,
`forever`, `permanent storage`, `fastest`, `best`, `unrivaled`, `unbeatable`,
`the most`, `world-class`. Every hit is reported with its file and line so a
human can judge it. The scan does not decide whether a hit is a claim or an
ordinary use of the word.

**Category 3 - unlabelled measurements.** A number followed by a unit (a
percentage, a time, a size, a read or base count, a throughput) with no
`SIMULATED` or `MEASURED` label in the nearby context. "Nearby" is
format-aware, so the label does not have to sit on the same line:

| format | context that counts as nearby |
| --- | --- |
| Markdown, reStructuredText | the paragraph plus its nearest heading |
| JSON | the enclosing top-level value |
| JSON Lines | the record, i.e. the line itself |
| anything else | the line and the two lines above it |

**Category 4 - credentials.** A `BEGIN ... PRIVATE KEY` block, a long hex
literal (16 or more hex characters) within 40 characters of a secret-ish word
(`token`, `secret`, `api_key`, `password`, `passwd`, `credential`), or an
`nvapi-` / `sk-` prefixed key. **The value is never printed.** A category-4 hit
is reported as file, line and kind only.

**Category 5 - scratch paths.** A temporary-directory or home-directory path in
a committed file.

## 2. How to run it

```
python tools/v15-evidence-scan.py --root .
```

It needs no network and nothing outside the standard library, it modifies no
file, and it exits 0 even when it finds hits. The other flags:

| flag | effect |
| --- | --- |
| `--quiet` | counts only, no hit list |
| `--markdown` | prints the result body of section 4, so this document can be regenerated |
| `--include-report` | also scans this report (see the note in section 5) |
| `--list-terms` | prints the search table and exits |

The search table (tool names, trailer phrases, scratch roots) is stored
base64-encoded in the script. That is deliberate: the committed source of a
hygiene scanner should not itself carry an AI-tool name, an attribution trailer
or a scratch path. `--list-terms` prints the table in the clear, so the scanner
can be audited without unpacking anything by hand.

## 3. Output conventions

Several literals are masked in the printed output, so that the output - and
this report - can be committed as-is without breaking the repository's own
hygiene rules:

| mask | replaces |
| --- | --- |
| `[AI-TOOL-NAME]` | an AI-tool, assistant or model name |
| `[TRAILER-TEXT]` | an attribution-trailer phrase |
| `[AI-SCRATCH-PATH]` | the agent scratch path |
| `[TMP]`, `[HOME]` | the leading directory of a scratch path; the rest of the path is kept |
| `[REDACTED]` | a long hex literal or a key-shaped token |

Every hit is still reported with its file, its line, the kind of hit, and the
surrounding text, so it can be judged. Where a literal is masked, the un-masked
literal is in the source file at the quoted line.

## Result on this tree

Files considered: **2440**; scanned as text: **2251**; skipped as binary: **187**.  The report file itself (`docs/V15_EVIDENCE_AUDIT.md`) is skipped by default because it quotes the hits it lists; `--include-report` scans it.

| category | what it looks for | hits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 attribution | AI-tool names, attribution trailers and the agent scratch path | **7** |
| 2 claims | synthesis / storage / sequencing claims, lifetime promises, superlatives | **4631** |
| 3 unlabelled measurements | a number presented as a measurement with no SIMULATED or MEASURED label near it | **5027** |
| 4 credentials | credential-looking literals (the value is never printed) | **7** |
| 5 scratch paths | temporary or home directory paths in committed files | **45** |
| | **total** | **9717** |

## 5. Reading the hits

The counts above are the honest counts. The notes below record what a first pass
of inspection saw, so that a reviewer knows where to start. They are not
clearances: every hit is still listed in section 4.

### Category 1 - attribution (7 hits, 2 files; 895 commit messages scanned)

* Six of the seven hits are on a single line, `experiments/v8/audit.py:118`.
  That line is the repository's own attribution gate: a case-insensitive regular
  expression of tool names and trailer phrases, applied to commit messages. The
  scan is reporting the scanner's own pattern. A human has to decide whether
  that line is the one place in the repository where the pattern has to be
  written out in full; it is the only committed file that contains tool names.
* One hit at `src/vnxdna/v2/stages.py:6`: the trailer phrase appears there in a
  technical sense (the inputs are produced with a named profile), not as an
  attribution trailer. A false positive of the phrase rule.
* The agent scratch path: **0 hits**. It does not appear in any committed file.
* Commit messages: **0 hits** across 895 commits. No tool name and no
  attribution trailer appears in any commit message in the committed history.

### Category 2 - claims (4631 hits, 375 files)

| term | hits | files |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `synthesised` | 2054 | 278 |
| `sequenced` | 2053 | 285 |
| `best` | 451 | 87 |
| `the most` | 26 | 18 |
| `forever` | 21 | 16 |
| `guaranteed` | 15 | 12 |
| `synthesized` | 8 | 5 |
| `fastest` | 3 | 3 |

* 4107 of the 4631 hits (88%) are the pair `synthesised` + `sequenced` in
  committed experiment result files, concentrated in
  `experiments/v9/coverage/results/envelope-cases.jsonl` (480),
  `experiments/v8/matrix/results/matrix.jsonl` (360) and
  `experiments/v9/coverage/results/eval.jsonl` (200). In those files the two
  words occur inside the standing disclaimer that no DNA was synthesised or
  sequenced. The scan cannot tell a disclaimer from a claim; a human should
  sample those files to confirm the wording is the disclaimer and only the
  disclaimer.
* `best` (451 hits, 87 files) is concentrated in selection and recovery code
  where it is an identifier: `src/vnxdna/recovery/outer_list.py` (32),
  `src/vnxdna/native/cpp/outerlist.cpp` (28),
  `src/vnxdna/native/c/cluster.c` (20).
* `the most` (26 hits) is ordinary English in prose and comments ("the most
  common read lengths", "the most expensive stage").
* `forever` (21 hits, 16 files) is mostly the Rust `Wait::Forever` enum variant
  (`src/vnxdna/native/rust/vnxd/src/ram.rs`, 5 hits) and comments of the form
  "never block forever" - the opposite of a lifetime promise.
* `guaranteed` (15 hits, 12 files) is used in the erasure-code sense.
  `docs/ECC.md:47` and `docs/ERROR_MODEL.md:41` define "Guaranteed" as a proven
  property of the code, not a guarantee on how long a medium keeps a record.
  `docs/V15_FINALIZATION_PLAN.md:1090` lists "any guaranteed lifetime or
  longevity figure" among the things that must not be claimed.
* `fastest` (3 hits) includes two of the repository's own tests that assert
  marketing superlatives are absent (`tests/v6/test_competitors.py:62`,
  `tests/providers/test_interop_docs.py:20`) and one use of `fastest` as the
  name of a redundancy profile (`tests/v6/test_redundancy_profiles.py:28`).

### Category 3 - unlabelled measurements (5027 hits, 618 files)

* By area: 2614 in `experiments/`, 1846 in `docs/`, 334 in `src/`, 197 in
  `tests/`, 21 in `CHANGELOG.md`, 15 in `README.md`.
* By format: 2332 Markdown, 898 `.log`, 855 plain text, 571 Python, 174 JSON,
  103 Rust, 71 CSV, 13 C, 6 shell, 2 C++, 1 JSON Lines, 1 include.
* The largest single contributors are `docs/DNA_STORAGE_DATASET_REGISTRY.md`
  (114 hits) and the older phase reports `docs/V5_PHASE4_REPORT.md` (98),
  `docs/V5_PHASE3_OPTIMIZATION.md` (82), `docs/V5_PHASE3_INDEL_RECOVERY.md`
  (75) and `docs/V5_PHASE2_NATIVE_ALIGNMENT.md` (70). The dataset registry
  counts numbers that describe other people's published datasets rather than
  VNX-DNA measurements.
* 898 hits are in raw run logs and 855 in plain text. A raw stdout log usually
  carries no SIMULATED label, so every number in it is reported. That is the
  rule working as specified; it is not 1753 unsupported numbers.
* This is the category where the definition of "nearby" matters most. The same
  scan with a different "nearby" gives: same line only, 7160 hits; the line and
  the one above, 7014; the line and the two above, 6892; the line and the five
  above, 6599; Markdown paragraph only, 4961; the format-aware rule used here,
  5027. The format-aware rule was chosen because it is the one a reader of the
  file would agree with, and the alternatives are listed so that a reviewer who
  prefers another definition can see how much it moves the number.

### Category 4 - credentials (7 hits, 3 files)

All seven are of kind `hex-literal-near-secret-word`. There is **no**
private-key block, **no** `nvapi-` prefixed key and **no** `sk-` prefixed key
anywhere in the committed tree. No credential value is printed by this scan or
by this report.

* Four in `src/vnxdna/native/rust/vnxd/src/authz.rs` (lines 263, 264, 342, 357)
  and two in `src/vnxdna/native/rust/vnxd/tests/e2e_matrix.rs` (lines 1266,
  1290): fixed test tokens - a reader token, an admin token and two
  wrong-token strings - each a 24 to 28 character hex literal sitting next to
  the word "token". They are test credentials for the authorisation module. The
  rule reports a hex literal next to "token" whether or not the literal is live,
  which is the behaviour it was written to have.
* One in `tests/v14/golden/contracts/messages.json:231`: a 64 character hex run
  inside a JSON-encoded IPC request in a golden fixture. That is a digest in a
  test vector, not a secret. A false positive of the rule.
* The `.gitleaksignore` list of reviewed test-key false positives names other
  files; none of its entries name these three. These seven hits are therefore
  not covered by an existing suppression, and a human should decide whether the
  Rust test tokens belong in one.

### Category 5 - scratch paths (45 hits, 20 files)

* 13 in `experiments/v8/fuzz/campaign-2026-10-07.txt` and 1 in the matching
  `.json`: the log path of a fuzz campaign.
* 9 in `docs/security/v11-redteam/sanitizers-align.txt`, 3 in
  `docs/security/v11-redteam/fuzz-campaigns.txt` and 1 in
  `docs/security/v11-redteam/pre-fix-measurements.txt`: security records that
  quote the temporary directory the campaign ran in.
* 2 in `docs/RELEASE_PROCESS.md:3` (a release recipe that builds into a
  temporary directory) and 1 each in `docs/SECURITY.md:100` (a note about
  predictable pytest temporary directories), `docs/HYBRID_ARCHITECTURE.md:174`,
  `docs/V10_COMPLETION_REPORT.md:42`, `docs/V11_BASELINE.md:21` and
  `docs/V5_COMPLETION_REPORT.md:148` (a sanitizer build directory).
* 2 in `docs/VNX_PRODUCT_STRATEGY.md:665,670`: the scan matched a `home` segment
  inside a `businesswire.com/news/...` URL path. Both are false positives.
* 2 in `tests/fixtures/v0_1/generate_fixtures.py:4,5` (a worktree checked out
  into a temporary directory), 1 in
  `tests/v14/integration/test_v14_e2e_python.py:163`, 1 in
  `src/vnxdna/native/rust/vnxd/src/nbdsys.rs:289` (a table of device paths in a
  Rust test), 1 in `experiments/v8/perf/results/profile.json:20` and 1 in each
  of the four `experiments/v5/phase3opt/**/results.json` files (the output path
  of a simulated run).
* Several of these hits also carry a lab-root path prefix before the temporary
  directory. The brief defines category 5 as temporary- and home-directory
  paths, so a lab-root prefix is out of scope for this category; it is worth a
  separate look.

### The report scans itself

This report is a committed file in `docs/`, and it quotes the hits it lists. The
scan therefore skips it by default and prints that it has done so. Running with
`--include-report` scans it as well: on this tree that reports **23,514** hits
instead of **9,717** - every hit quoted above a second time, plus the hits in
the prose of this document. The exact figure moves as this document is edited,
so re-run the command rather than trusting the number written here. The counts
in section 4 are the counts for the tree without this report.

## 6. What this scan does not cover

* It is a text scan. 187 committed files are binary and are skipped, so a key
  inside a PDF, an image or a compiled artefact would not be seen.
* It matches words, not meaning. It cannot tell the standing disclaimer in a
  results file from a real claim, and it cannot tell a test token from a live
  one. That is what a human is for.
* It does not check whether a number is traceable to a committed results file.
  It only checks for a nearby label.
* It does not check the commit author, the branch state, the test count, or any
  other release-hygiene item.
* It does not scan outside the scope in section 1. `tools/` is not in scope, and
  neither is any file that is not committed.
* It modifies nothing, needs no network, and does not fail a build. It is a
  report, not a gate.
